Hybrid TES RTU system - results and discussion The 24-hour simulation results are shown in Figures 23 and 24 for Los Angeles and Baltimore, respectively. There are six sets of graphs in each figure, including (a) one for the baseline RTU, and (b) five for the hybrid TES RTU. The black dashed lines show the assumed 6 h peak-demand period between noon and 6pm. The graph for the baseline RTU shows the total HVAC load and the heat absorbed by the evaporator, which meets the HVAC load, including cycling to meet the load during low-load periods. The blue line shows the total RTU power, which reaches its peak during the peak- demand period. The five graphs for the hybrid TES RTU show the same HVAC load as the baseline, the heat absorbed by the cooling coil, which meets this HVAC load, and the RTU energy use (blue line). These five plots also show the heat transfer into the boiling refrigerant (light blue line), and the heat being storage in the TES (dashed grey line). The control strategy charges the TES from the initial 25% to ~85%, and then maintains that SOC until just before the peak period. This keeps the evaporator temperature lower, and improves heat-pump efficiency during the morning hours where cooling is needed, but the battery is not being charged or discharged. The TES is then charged to >95% just before noon. During the peak period, the compressor speed changes to maintain a constant power for the entire RTU (compressor + fans + pump).
